channel.title: The Kimberley Echo - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Kimberley Echo (kimberleyecho.com.au)

item.title: Cluster caterpillars develop resistance to common insecticides in Kununurra and Broome
item.description: The cluster caterpillar, a widespread pest, is now resisting commonly used insecticides in Kununurra and Broome, according to the Department of Primary Industries and Regional Development.

item.title: WATCH: Teenagers roll allegedly stolen ute in Halls Creek
item.description: Dramatic footage from the East Kimberley shows teenagers flipping an allegedly stolen ute as they race towards police in Halls Creek.

item.title: Kimberley fracking project ‘most highly contested EPA decision in WA history’
item.description: An “unprecedented” number of appeals have been lodged against the EPA’s recommendation to approve the Valhalla Gas Exploration Program in the Kimberley, according to the Office of the Appeals Convenor.

item.title: Shire of Halls Creek responds to scathing Auditor General report
item.description: The Shire of Halls Creek has responded to the recent scathing Auditor General’s report which found the local government authority had missed financial reporting deadlines for the past five years.

item.title: Kununurra’s Bolten family in running to be named most innovative farmers in Australia
item.description: Kununurra’s Bolten family are finalists in The Weekly Times Coles 2025 Farmer of the Year Awards, for their dedication to finding a crop with longevity in a challenging region.

item.title: Kimberley youth called to Parliament program
item.description: Young people from across the Kimberley are being urged to put their hand up for the Y WA’s Youth Parliament program, with applications now open for the program’s 31st year

item.title: Walking to wellbeing
item.description: Staff from across the Kimberley Land Council rack up close to 12 million steps during organisation’s end of year step challenge

item.title: Kimberley kids are back at school
item.description: Kids across the Kimberley headed back to school, with remote communities marking the start of term through culture and connection.

item.title: Updated Regional Airfare Zone Cap bookings now available for flights after July 1
item.description: Reduced airfares for remote residents under the updated Regional Airfare Zone Cap scheme are now open for the second half of 2026.

item.title: Durack MP Melissa Price backs new Liberal leader Angus Taylor
item.description: Durack MP Melissa Price has thrown her support behind new Liberal leader Angus Taylor after losing her bid to become the party’s deputy leader on February 13.
